cells.tense: You have your hands on this and the hands are working — you feel when to add and when to ease off.
cells.ask: Find one spot today where give and take have gone lopsided, and do the small visible thing that squares them — no tally, just that one move — and watch whether the fairness starts moving on its own.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day this is you moving through the people close to you and nudging the temperature of a conversation, an evening, a plan — adding a little, subtracting a little, and knowing why. You've kept something steady through a change that could have taken it, and it still stands because you keep it standing.

What's open now is where it goes from here. The way back into fuller flow is what fair exchange does, and that means one spot where the give and take has slid out of true. You're not being told to hand over more; you're being asked to look at one place today and square it, which is a move you already make well.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it steady through the change, and you're still the one adjusting it.
cells.verb: hold the shape of what the change left behind and keep it standing
cells.place: the place where you keep adjusting the mix to keep it flowing

cells.tense: A good part of you lives in a future where this needs defending, and you're guarding something nothing has threatened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've already settled, and leave it exactly as it is for a day — no adjusting, no extra grip — then notice what it did without your hand.
cells.core:
There are days here when you check the temperature, make the small correction, and then leave it alone — you read the room, adjust, and let it be, because part of keeping something is not gripping it. The grip stays light and the thing you built stays standing on its own.

The adjusting has gone past checking. An arrangement, a closeness, a thing you made, hasn't happened yet, and you're already bracing for it — tightening, moving pieces before they've moved. The worry is spending you on a day that hasn't arrived. Loosen one grip today and let it show you whether it needed your hands at all.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping this tighter than it needs, for a threat that isn't here yet.
cells.verb: hold the shape of what the change left behind and keep it standing
cells.place: the place where you keep adjusting the mix to keep it flowing

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you, hand on the knob.
cells.ask: Do one thing today that only makes sense if the change is finished — say yes to one small plan, or move one object into where you actually live now — and let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You adjust to what's actually in front of you — reading the day, adding and subtracting as it comes — and your choices carry a direction that comes from what you genuinely feel rather than from what you're bracing against. That's the ordinary version.

The adjusting has stopped. There's no mix to work with, because you haven't fully turned toward what's here; the pull of what was keeps your attention behind you. It isn't steady feeling that's absent. It's direction you've chosen and are willing to stand in — and that comes back by moving, not by feeling steadier first. One small step toward now tends to show you which way you're pointed.
cells.sheetLine: You're still adjusting for a room you've already left.
cells.verb: hold the shape of what the change left behind and keep it standing

cells.tense: Something here stays steady because of adjustments you make without calling them yours.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, one structure you're maintaining — the routine, the arrangement, the way this runs — and name yourself plainly as the one holding it.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day this looks like things going smoothly around you — the plan that comes together, the people who know where they stand, the day that runs — and none of it gets framed as your doing, because it just works.

But the work is there. You've been the one reaching into the mix, sensing when something needs adding or taking away, and keeping what the change left standing. You'd say the situation runs that way by itself. It runs that way because you've been at it, and saying so out loud is how the credit and the choice come back to you.
